model_interpretation.claim: The previous valid OpenMP candidate used a serial cutoff of 512 options per requested worker. Lowering the cutoff to 256 options per effective worker, while limiting the requested team to min(threads, n), tests whether parallelizing medium workloads pays off without creating idle workers or exceeding the passed CPU budget. The controller must measure the cutoff's overhead and any gain; no result is assumed here.

A serial path for one thread and fewer than 512 options per requested thread should avoid paying parallel-region overhead on small workloads. Each loop iteration writes exactly its own result index; the controller still needs to verify correctness and measure the tradeoff.

items.subject: OpenMP scaling and overhead within the threads budget
items.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, compare the serial baseline with an OpenMP outer loop using the passed threads value as a hard CPU budget; start with static scheduling and retain a serial path for one thread or small n. Avoid thresholds tied to published test values. Measure available valid n/thread cases under the frozen protocol, verify complete output writes and varied-input correctness, and report overhead as well as any gain. Preserve correct variants for later combination even if they lose in isolation.
